title: Cache Stampede
subtitle: Mitigating dogpiling and thundering herds using Singleflight Request Coalescing, Distributed Leases, and XFetch.
keyTakeaways: A Cache Stampede (thundering herd) occurs when a hot cache entry expires and thousands of concurrent requests miss simultaneously, all hitting the database at once.
In-process Request Coalescing (Singleflight) ensures that only one database query executes per application server regardless of how many concurrent requests arrive.
The XFetch probabilistic early expiration algorithm recalculates and refreshes the cache entry before it expires based on its generation time and remaining TTL.
architectureDiagram:
CACHE STAMPEDE (THUNDERING HERD) VS SINGLEFLIGHT
WITHOUT MITIGATION (5,000 Concurrent Misses -> Database Meltdown):
[ 5,000 Requests ] ---> (Cache Miss on Expired Key) ---> [ 5,000 Concurrent DB Queries ] (DB Crashes!)

WITH SINGLEFLIGHT REQUEST COALESCING:
[ 5,000 Requests ] ---> [ Singleflight Mutex ] ---> 1 Query to Database
                                  |
                                  +---> Other 4,999 requests wait on the same Promise/Channel

sections.heading: Request Coalescing (Singleflight) and Distributed Mutexes
sections.body: When an expensive cached object (e.g., an aggregated home dashboard requiring 15 SQL JOINs) expires under 10,000 requests per second, every incoming thread experiences a cache miss. All 10,000 threads simultaneously attempt to execute the expensive query against the database, causing connection pool exhaustion, CPU saturation, and cascading timeouts.
bullets: In-Process Singleflight (Go/Node.js): If 500 requests on Server 1 miss the cache for the same key, Singleflight ensures only the first request queries the database. The other 499 requests block and subscribe to the identical in-flight Promise or channel.

Distributed Mutex / Leases: In a multi-server cluster, use Redis `SET lock:key token NX EX 10` to elect a single worker across the entire fleet to refresh the database, while other workers sleep briefly or return stale data.
Return Stale While Revalidating: Serve the expiring cached data for an extra 30 seconds while an asynchronous background worker computes the fresh replacement.

sections.heading: Probabilistic Early Expiration: The XFetch Algorithm
sections.body: Instead of waiting for a hot key to expire and risking a stampede, the optimal strategy is refreshing the key before expiration. However, static early refresh triggers unnecessary computation. The XFetch algorithm computes a probabilistic early refresh based on the time it took to generate the cache entry (`computeTime`), the remaining TTL, and an aggressive multiplier (`beta`).
bullets: XFetch Formula: Recompute if `-beta * computeTime * ln(random()) > remainingTtl`.
Dynamic Probabilistic Scaling: As the key gets closer to its expiration timestamp, the probability of a reader triggering a background refresh approaches 1.0.
Zero Stampede: Exactly one reader probabilistically triggers the refresh shortly before expiry, keeping the cache continuously warm without downtime.

tradeOffs.pros: Zero distributed locking complexity; collapses thousands of concurrent in-process calls into 1 query; zero staleness.
tradeOffs.cons: Protects only within an individual container; if you run 200 containers, 200 database queries still execute concurrently.
tradeOffs.bestFor: Node.js, Go, and Java web servers under heavy concurrent read volume.

tradeOffs.pros: Keys never expire for users; eliminates read-path cache misses entirely for active hot keys.
tradeOffs.cons: Requires storing generation duration metadata alongside cached values; slightly higher cache writes.
tradeOffs.bestFor: Extremely expensive computational queries (dashboard aggregations, reporting tables, leaderboard snapshots).

interviewTip: To stand out in high-concurrency caching discussions, introduce Singleflight and XFetch: 'To prevent cache stampedes when hot keys expire, we combine in-process Singleflight request coalescing to collapse concurrent misses into a single database query, paired with the XFetch algorithm to probabilistically refresh hot keys before they expire.'
